clue.text: Student initially losing pound as paid employee

indicators.note: the student word drops its opening letter, which is the one standing for pound

parts.note: a student is a learner
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A student starts work after losing money, becoming a paid employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who earns a wage is an earner, so a paid employee fits by synonym.

clue.text: Restaurants serving various teas around lake

indicators.note: around says the shuffled teas letters wrap the lake
various suggests the letters of teas in a mixed order

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Restaurants by a lakeside serve a selection of teas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' is a link word, and the lake is one of North America's Great Lakes rather than an L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eateries is an informal word for places serving food, i.e. restaurants.

clue.text: Family member who's kept in order?

definitions.meaning: a female sibling within a family
a nun, a member of a religious order

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a female sibling and a nun belonging to a religious order.

clue.text: Organist composed 14, 17, or 19

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters of the referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: 14 refers to the answer at 14 across, a Greek wine

explanation.surface: An organist wrote music numbered 14, 17 or 19.
explanation.walkthrough: Any of the answers at 14, 17 or 19 rearranges to the answer, which is why all three are offered. Sir John Stainer was a Victorian organist and composer, of The Crucifixion.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stainer was a famous English church organist and composer.

clue.text: State forcefully includes king in what's beneficial

indicators.note: includes says the beneficial word holds the king's letter inside it

parts.note: an asset is something beneficial or useful
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone declares firmly that having a king is beneficial.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to declare it firmly, which is stating forcefully.

clue.text: Send up stuff about pupil's surroundings

indicators.note: about says the word for stuff goes round the other piece

parts.note: to sate is to stuff or glut
the iris is the coloured ring surrounding the pupil of the eye

explanation.surface: A schoolchild gets teased over the things around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild, but it is the eye's pupil, ringed by the IRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up someone is to mock them, which is what satirising does.

clue.text: They won't complain about diabolical service

definitions.text: They won't complain about diabolical service

parts.words: They won't complain about diabolical service
parts.note: a diabolical service sounds like awful customer care, but read literally it is a devil-worshipping rite, which its own congregation would welcome

explanation.definitionFit: Devil worshippers attend diabolical rites gladly, so they are the ones who won't complain.

clue.text: Person from Japan or China I saw returning

annotationWithheld.why: Person from Japan or China I saw returning (5): the run is hidden reversed in 'China I saw', but no word signals the hiding besides 'returning', which already signals the reversal; read as 'Person from Japan or China', the word China would be both definition and fodder
annotationWithheld.clue: Person from Japan or China I saw returning

clue.text: Give consideration to host

definitions.meaning: to think about an idea, as in considering a proposal
to receive guests and look after them

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to consider an idea and to receive guests as host.

clue.text: Near end of holiday, one's taken in second test

indicators.note: taken in says the letter for one is placed inside the holiday word, near its end

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Near the end of a holiday, a student must take an exam again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near end of' tells you where the I goes: just before the last letter of REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an examination taken a second time after failing.

clue.text: Gossip about new girl

indicators.note: about says the gossip word is placed round the letter for new

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or gossip about a person

explanation.surface: People chatter about a girl who has just arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of sayings and gossip, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a girl's name, and the clue uses girl for any female first name.

clue.text: Having row with contrary painter that's less of a Philistine

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the painter's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone argues with an awkward painter who is more cultured than a boor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats; a Philistine is someone hostile to the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Philistine scorns culture, so someone artier is more artistic and less of one.

clue.text: Genius of the naughty nineties?

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters of the following word misbehave and get jumbled

explanation.surface: A clever spark from the wild 1890s.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'naughty nineties' (the 1890s) is a stock phrase; 'naughty' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used generically for any genius.

clue.text: Wine that gets 4, 17, or 19 drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, the organist

explanation.surface: A wine that gets an organist or others drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Any of 4, 17 or 19 rearranges to this resinated Greek wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Quality that to a considerable extent is queer, in essence

indicators.note: the answer makes up most of the following words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A quality that, in essence, is mostly queer.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'queer, in essence', taking up most of it, which is what 'to a considerable extent' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eeriness is the strange, unsettling quality of something, a characteristic.

clue.text: Intimate approach

definitions.meaning: close or dear, as a close friend

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both close in relationship and, as a verb, to come closer.

clue.text: Distortion of 4, 14, or 19 is not so pleasant

indicators.note: a distortion twists the shape, so the referenced answer's letters are rearranged

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, the organist

explanation.surface: Distorting one of these answers makes it less pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, so it means less pleasant.

clue.text: Salt, ie sailor, given special treat

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: special suggests the letters of treat arranged in a particular new way

explanation.surface: A salty sailor gets special treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like the old sailor, but it is the chemical; 'special' makes TRATE from TREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartrate is a salt of tartaric acid, as in cream of tartar.

clue.text: Keeps modifying 4, 14, or 17

indicators.note: modifying means changing, so the letters of the referenced answer are rearranged

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4 down, the organist

explanation.surface: One keeps altering these numbered answers.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to keep hold of it.

clue.text: Furious about ceremony being shortened? Bother!

indicators.note: about says the furious word goes round the cut-down ceremony

parts.note: irate means furious

indicators.note: being shortened says the ceremony word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a ritual short in fury and exclaims in annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bother!' is the verb as an exclamation, as in 'Don't bother me!'; 'being shortened' drops the final letter of the ceremony word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother someone is to annoy them, which is to irritate.

clue.text: Not reacting about son being put inside

indicators.note: about says the inactive word is placed round the son's letter

parts.note: inert describes a substance that does not react chemically

explanation.surface: A passive son is being sent to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to place something inside something else.

clue.text: Worry that people may dispute in controversy

definitions.text: that people may dispute in controversy
definitions.meaning: speakers argue whether the word controversy is said with emphasis on its first or second syllable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both anxiety and the emphasis on a syllable, which is disputed in that word.

clue.text: A piece of cake for person at table

definitions.meaning: an easy chance, such as a catch no fielder should drop
someone seated, as a diner seated at a table

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an easy opportunity and one who sits, such as at a table.

clue.text: Behind a lot of bones found in chests

parts.note: the stern is the rear, or behind, of a ship

explanation.surface: Lots of bones are found behind a chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lot of' is a link; 'chests' are rib cages, not boxes. The answer is the plural of sternum, the breastbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Mediterranean plant propagated in sea

indicators.note: propagated, as in growing a plant afresh, signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean plant grows in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is a Mediterranean plant grown for its liquorice-tasting seeds.

clue.text: New Yorker, for example, creates attention about a humorous author

indicators.note: about says the attention word goes round the author

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
Laurence Sterne wrote the comic novel Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A New York writer draws attention to a comic author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Yorker' suggests the magazine, but means a person from the East Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from New York lives in the eastern USA, an example of an easterner.

clue.text: Peters out after 1762, for example

parts.note: Peter III of Russia was deposed in 1762, and with him the line of rulers called Peter ended, so these monarchs ran out of Peters

explanation.definitionFit: Peter the Great and Peter III were Russian emperors, and none later bore the name.

clue.text: I test nine or ten in site developed for part of vital canal

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone checks nine or ten sites developed for a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I test nine' is also an anagram of the answer, offered as an alternative to 'ten in site'; either works with 'developed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestine is part of the alimentary canal, essential to life.
